title: The Possession of Wisdom and the Exodus of the Soul
english: A proverb is a word which, through sensible things, signifies intelligible matters.

The kingdom of Israel is spiritual knowledge containing discourses about God, the incorporeal and the corporeal, judgment, and providence, or revealing a theory concerning the ethical, the physical, and the theological.

For the purpose of knowing wisdom and instruction, he says, 'reigned in Israel to know instruction and wisdom' (Prov 1:2). And wisdom is the knowledge of bodies and incorporeal things and the judgment and providence observed in these; but instruction is the moderation of passions, observing the passionate or irrational part of the soul.

To direct judgment: The judgment to be direct and incorruptible signifies the criterion. And there are three criteria in us: sensation, word, and mind; sensation indeed of the sensible, word of names and utterances and things said, but mind of the intelligible.
And piety toward God is the beginning of sensation: Just as through sensations the mind imposes itself upon the sensible, so also through virtues it presides over the intelligible.
But the impious will despise wisdom and instruction: Those who cultivate wickedness will despise wisdom and instruction; but by word, as I think, no one despises wisdom and instruction.

For a crown of grace will be on your head and a golden ring around your neck: Just as the head and the neck signify the mind there, so also the crown and the ring signify knowledge there. For this is the custom of the Holy Spirit to name God and his angels, and the mind, and virtue, and knowledge, and wickedness, and ignorance, and the devil himself and his angels, with many names. But he does not set down the names simply, as some think; for they are identifiers of different activities, of God through his angels working in us and of us in him, and of demons.

The possession of the righteous is wisdom, understanding, and prudence. The impious seize this possession, persuading the righteous to do something of those things forbidden by God, so that the mind, having been blinded by sin, may fall from these holy estates. These are plundered by those whom the demons conquer, taking from them the panoply of God: the helmet, the breastplate, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God (Eph 6:16-17).

Those who are co-heirs with the adversaries are they who partake of the same wickedness as them. For that which is not of the One God is common. Nets are not spread unjustly; it is a net, an eternal punishment from the righteous Judge, drawn toward the impure souls to their destruction as they flee badly with their wings.

Wisdom is praised in exoduses; in the marketplaces it leads to boldness; on the tops of walls it is proclaimed; and at the gates of the powerful it sits. Exodus now names the soul emerging from wickedness and ignorance. Such is also the exodus of the sons of Israel, which has come to pass after the generation of the judgment and teaching of God. Regarding the same soul, he says: 'Enlarge the place of your tent' (Isa 54:2) and 'Enlarge your heart' (2 Cor 6:13) in the address of Paul to the Corinthians. And wisdom is praised by the soul emerging in this way; and in the soul being enlarged through virtues, it leads to boldness. Its high wall he calls the highest apathy, if 'those who love the law surround themselves with a wall' (Ps 50:14), for which wall David also prays, saying: 'Let the walls be built.'
